name: Commercial energy cost management for ComEd-zone food, cold-storage and multi-site grocery accounts (supply procurement + capacity-tag management + demand-response origination + bill audit) (post-review)
summary: POST-REVIEW MODEL. Stage E assumptions with the Stage F adversarial reviewer's corrected drivers applied. Corrected base (review §1/§4 'Reviewer base'): sales cycle 10 months (contract-expiry wait), 7 qualified exempt-size conversations/month, 20% proposal->win, ARPC $800 (DR share ~0). Optimistic = reviewer upside exactly (cycle 8, 9 leads, 22% win, ARPC $900, all other drivers at base). Conservative = Stage E conservative with reviewer's cycle 12 and 5 leads layered on (reviewer's ARPC $650 and churn 1.8% are milder than filed, so filed $460 / 2.0% kept). Original Stage E model: SYN-004_assumptions.json (unchanged).
evidence_notes: STAGE F CORRECTIONS (07_review/SYN-004_review.md): sales_cycle_months 6/4/3 -> 12/10/8; founder_leads_per_month 6/10/12 -> 5/7/9; proposal_to_win_pct 0.15/0.22/0.28 -> 0.15/0.20/0.22; arpc_monthly 460/850/1380 -> 460/800/900; optimistic scenario := reviewer upside (other drivers at base); reviewer's own conservative (base drivers + cycle 12, leads 5, win 15%, ARPC 650, churn 1.8%) reported separately: Y3 -$2.7k, Y5 $30.4k, peak $212.6k

Licensing (A): 83 IAC 454.30(b)(5) - Part 454 does not apply to any person who attempts to procure retail electric service on behalf of, or sell it to, a third party with aggregate billing demand of all affiliated Illinois accounts >1,500 kW; 'aggregate billing demand' = total of the highest monthly billed demand of each affiliated account in the past calendar year (454.20); rule last amended 35 Ill. Reg. 17602, eff. 2011-11-01 (E-SYN004-S001, S002, S003). Statute 220 ILCS 5/16-115C(b) wording seen only via search snippets (ilga.gov unreachable) - confirm (E-SYN004-S004).

Supplier onboarding (B): ENGIE asks for years of energy experience, number of customers represented, state licence copies, credit score and legal review of marketing; its 2025 remittance agreement pays the broker fee monthly on the 25th only after the customer pays, with consumption true-ups and no payment after a terminated customer agreement (E-SYN004-S006, S007).

Broker fee level (D): Chicago BOMA deck shows supplier offers of $0.001-$0.005/kWh (DI-S026); an Illinois school district estimated an outside broker at ~3 mils (~$13k/yr) (E-SYN004-S011, search summary). Exempt customers use >=7 GWh/yr (1.5 MW x 8,760 h x ~0.55-0.65 load factor, E), and mils fall with size (C7-S009), so base = 1.0 mil on 9 GWh (E).

Capacity price (A): FERC accepted the price collar for the 2029/30 BRA too: cap $337.83, floor $181.91/MW-day UCAP; COMED CETL/CETO < 1 and COMED CETL -68% (E-SYN004-S008, S009). Capacity value is bounded through May 2030; after that it is unknown, so no price growth in base.

DR split (A/C/D): customer kept 70-75% in a 2020 Illinois packet (DI-S023); a 2025 PJM DR guide says the CSP share is usually 20-40%, negotiable (E-SYN004-S012, C); vendors now advertise 100% pass-through with a fixed fee or a guaranteed $73k/MW-yr floor (E-SYN004-S013, S014, D). A channel partner's cut must come from a shrinking CSP margin: 3% / 6% / 10% of gross (E, MISSING). DR UCAP/ICAP ~0.91 in the 2028/29 BRA (E-SYN004-S010, A).
PLC and DR overlap (D): nominated DR value = PLC minus firm service level (E-SYN004-S014), so the same kW cannot be sold twice; the ARPC blend applies DR and PLC fees to different account subsets.

Funnel, churn, splits, audit hit rates, CSP partner share and all staffing productivity are E. Hiring is gated on revenue/accounts (not calendar) so the conservative case shows a founder-only business rather than a runaway loss.

drivers.sales_start_delay_months__source: LLC + insurance + supplier onboarding: ENGIE replies within 15 business days, then nine documents incl. credit score, licence copies and legal review of marketing (DI-S027, E-SYN004-S006, S007) + CSP partner agreement. No ABC licence needed for the >1,500 kW segment (E-SYN004-S001).
drivers.sales_cycle_months__source: STAGE F CORRECTION: 07_review/SYN-004_review.md §2 F5 and §4: fee starts only when the new supply contract flows at the customer's current expiry (ENGIE pays nothing until a Customer Agreement is executed and the customer pays [B, F2-S005]); ~3 months selling + ~9-month average expiry wait -> 10 base / 12 conservative / 8 upside (E). Biggest error in the Stage E model | Stage E source: Revenue starts only when the new supply contract flows; large C&I contracts run 12-36 months, so a signed mandate often waits for expiry. Stage D expected many targets locked into 2028-29 expiries. DR enrolment follows delivery-year deadlines (DR payments annual, mid-July; E-SYN004-S012).
drivers.founder_leads_per_month__source: STAGE F CORRECTION: 07_review/SYN-004_review.md §4: courted, already-brokered exempt pool (93% of >1 MW ComEd usage on ARES [A, F2-S008]); must screen kW before pitching; no track record (E): 10 -> 7 base / 5 conservative / 9 upside | Stage E source: Correction (Stage E): qualified conversations with exempt-size (>1,500 kW aggregate) decision makers that yield 12 months of bills/interval data. Stage D's 22/month suited small accounts; the exempt pool is a few thousand Illinois customers, many on corporate procurement. Target lists: Chicago benchmarking (E-SYN004-S015), EPA ECHO food/cold storage (DI-S017/S018).
drivers.lead_to_proposal_pct__source: Free PLC/bill audit converts to an RFP or DR proposal; analyst estimate.
drivers.proposal_to_win_pct__source: STAGE F CORRECTION: 07_review/SYN-004_review.md §4: every win displaces an incumbent broker; customer designates between brokers [B, F2-S005] (E): 22% -> 20% base / 15% conservative / 22% upside | Stage E source: Heavily courted segment (392 ABCs; >1 MW customers 93% switched, C7-S007); ENGIE may contact the customer directly and lets the customer pick between competing brokers (E-SYN004-S007). Analyst estimate.
drivers.rep_new_customers_per_month__source: Correction (Stage E): large exempt accounts, not 1.5/month small accounts. Analyst estimate.
drivers.referral_new_per_100_active__source: Refrigeration contractors, CPAs, trade associations (MWFPA directory, DI-S032). Analyst estimate.
drivers.monthly_churn_pct__source: STAGE F CORRECTION: 07_review/SYN-004_review.md §4: churn 1.2% kept as reasonable; reviewer conservative 1.8% is milder than filed 2.0%, so filed 2.0% kept | Stage E source: ~20-30% lost at each 12-36-month renewal => ~1-2%/month; ENGIE stops paying the broker fee if the customer agreement terminates (E-SYN004-S007); active ComEd ARES -14% y/y (C7-S007).
drivers.arpc_monthly__source: STAGE F CORRECTION: 07_review/SYN-004_review.md §3/§4: DR partner share ~0 (CSPs advertise 100% pass-through [D, F2-S010]) and true-ups [B]: $850 -> $800 base / upside $900; conservative keeps the filed $460 (harsher than the reviewer's $650) | Stage E source: Base: 9 GWh x $0.0010 = $750/mo supply fee + DR partner share on 20% of accounts (0.4 MW x 0.91 UCAP x $325 x 365 x 6% = $2,591/site/yr => $43/mo) + PLC fee on 25% of accounts (150 kW x $325 x 365 x 15% = $2,669/yr => $56/mo). Conservative: 7 GWh x 0.75 mil + DR 15% x 0.3 MW x $250 avg x 3% + PLC 15% x 100 kW x 12% = $460. Optimistic: 11 GWh x 1.25 mils ($1,146) + DR 25% x 0.5 MW x 0.91 x $330 x 10% ($114) + PLC 30% x 200 kW x $330 x 20% ($120) = $1,380 (an upper bound, not a plan). Prices A (E-SYN004-S008, DI-S022); UCAP factor A (E-SYN004-S010); mils D (DI-S026, E-SYN004-S011); partner share E (MISSING).
drivers.onetime_revenue_per_new_customer__source: Contingency audit hits (~30% x ~$6k x ~35%, WS11-010) plus occasional supplier upfront payments ($12-18k upfront offers exist with lower residuals, DI-S026). Hit rates MISSING.
drivers.arpc_annual_growth_pct__source: Mils are fixed per contract; capacity collared $175-$338/MW-day through May 2030 (E-SYN004-S008, S009); conservative assumes renewal mils compression and post-2030 capacity falling toward the floor.
drivers.gross_margin_pct__source: Supplier-remitted fees are near-pure margin, but early or sub-1,500 kW deals may run through a licensed partner ABC at a ~50% split (split MISSING), and ENGIE-type agreements true-up fees to actual consumption and withhold them when customers do not pay (E-SYN004-S007).
drivers.onetime_gross_margin_pct__source: Audit data extraction cost only; analyst estimate.
drivers.variable_opex_pct_revenue__source: Payment processing, data pulls; analyst estimate.
drivers.cac_per_new_customer__source: Site visits, travel, interval-data pulls, trade events per large account won; analyst estimate.
drivers.fixed_marketing_per_month__source: Food-industry/cold-chain association dues and events, website; analyst estimate.
drivers.dso_days__source: ENGIE remits on the 25th of the month after the customer pays and withholds if unpaid (E-SYN004-S007, B); DR paid once a year, typically mid-July (E-SYN004-S012, C).
drivers.dpo_days__source: Partner splits paid after receipt; analyst estimate.
drivers.tax_rate_pct__source: Stage E standardization rule (simplified blended pass-through rate).
drivers.founder_draw_per_month__source: Stage E standardization rule: $4,000/mo living stipend from month 13 in all scenarios.
drivers.start_capital_injection__source: Stage E standardization rule re-applied to the post-review base: smallest round injection keeping base cash >= 0 (REV base peak funding rounded up to $100). Does not change operating profit, FCF or peak funding.
drivers.lt_growth_y6_pct__source: Illinois ARES non-residential supply fell 1.5% and ComEd non-residential ARES customers were flat in 2026 (C7-S007/ORMD 2026), so years 6-10 growth is share gain only; capacity collar ends with 2029/30 (E-SYN004-S008). Conservative 0%.
drivers.lt_growth_decay__source: Illinois-only exempt pool saturates; analyst assumption.
drivers.incremental_roic_pct__source: Growth capital is a rep's 6-month ramp (~$39k) plus receivables (~2 months of revenue); a productive rep adds ~7 large accounts/yr (~$70k/yr fee revenue at base ARPC). ~1.0x pre-tax base; 0.5x conservative (new states need new licences/supplier approvals).
drivers.maint_capex_pct_op__source: Laptops, kW data loggers, software seats; analyst estimate.
drivers.reserve_months__source: Fees stop when a customer agreement terminates and are trued-up to actual use (E-SYN004-S007); 3 months in conservative for supplier-exit/clawback shocks.
drivers.ev_multiple__source: Multiple of op before owner pay (SDE-like). Energy-book multiples MISSING. Anchors: small insurance books 5-7x profit with earn-outs (C5-S021, C) - a ceiling, because insurance renews annually while energy contracts re-bid every 1-3 years; owner-operated Chicago-suburb service business asked ~3.2x SDE (DF-S004, D). Founder-dependent, supplier-terminable book discounted to 2.5x.

staff.role: Licence-qualifying compliance partner (part-time retainer; named in an ABC application under 454.70 to open the <1,500 kW segment)
staff.notes: E: hired only once monthly revenue >= $8k proves the exempt book. ABC licence needs 1 yr electric-industry experience of the persons used (C7-S001); whether the founder's own exempt-segment year counts is unverified.

staff.role: Energy analyst (bill/interval data, RFP administration, PLC alerts, DR performance)
staff.notes: E: loaded cost; founder does analysis until 35 large accounts.
C/E: BLS OEWS 2025 Chicago non-technical wholesale sales reps mean $85,490 (DI-S015); lower base + commission. Correction (Stage E): hired at $25k/mo revenue, not at a fixed month 18.
